The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ōkuninushi|lt_ja=大己貴神}} In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “{{ill|Prefecture Lord|ja|県主|lt=Prefecture Lord|lt_ja=県}} (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}} – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the {{ill|Shinsen Seishiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of {{ill|Sendai Kojihonki|ja|先代旧事本紀}} he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城}} – active during the {{ill|Jimmu Eastern Expedition|ja|神武東征}} – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenpyo|ja|天平}} (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of {{ill|Daido|ja|大同}} (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄}}, 12 households from {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}} were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in {{ill|Rokukokushi|ja|六国史|lt=National History|lt_ja=国史}}, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenan|ja|天安 (日本)|lt=Tenan|lt_ja=天安}} (859) the divine rank ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Shinkai|ja|神階}}) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|lt=Enchō}} (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of {{ill|Bunmei|ja|文明}} (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, under the modern shrine ranking system ({{ill|Modern Shrine Ranking System|ja|近代社格制度}}) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenan|ja|天安 (日本)|lt=Tenan|lt_ja=天安}} (859), on {{ill|January 27|ja|1月27日}}, the divine rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} as having been established by the 10th-generation {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名}}, Heibonsha, 1981. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社}}. ==Enshrined Deities==

The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ōkuninushi|lt_ja=大己貴神}} In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “{{ill|Prefecture Lord|ja|県主|lt=Prefecture Lord|lt_ja=県}} (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}} – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the {{ill|Shinsen Seishiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of {{ill|Sendai Kojihonki|ja|先代旧事本紀}} he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城}} – active during the {{ill|Jimmu Eastern Expedition|ja|神武東征}} – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenpyo|ja|天平}} (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of {{ill|Daido|ja|大同}} (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄}}, 12 households from {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}} were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in {{ill|Rokukokushi|ja|六国史|lt=National History|lt_ja=国史}}, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenan|ja|天安 (日本)|lt=Tenan|lt_ja=天安}} (859) the divine rank ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Shinkai|ja|神階}}) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|lt=Enchō}} (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of {{ill|Bunmei|ja|文明}} (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, under the modern shrine ranking system ({{ill|Modern Shrine Ranking System|ja|近代社格制度}}) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenan|ja|天安 (日本)|lt=Tenan|lt_ja=天安}} (859), on {{ill|January 27|ja|1月27日}}, the divine rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} as having been established by the 10th-generation {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|ja|大神神社}}).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to {{ill|Ise Jingu|ja|伊勢神宮}}. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Ponsonby-Fane |first=R. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Army |first=United States Department of the |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PvgsAAAAIAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=RA3-PA147 |title=Pamphlet - Dept. of the Army |date=1945 |publisher=Headquarters, Department of the Army. |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MVHoAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA147 |title=Department of the Army Pamphlet |date=1945 |publisher=The Department |language=en}} ==Overview== {{神社 |名称 = 志貴御縣坐神社 |image = {{ill|File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg|ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg}}|280px
Haiden |所在地 = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}{{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}} Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ōkuninushi|lt_ja=大己貴神}} |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a shrine located at Kanaya 896 in {{ill|Sakurai City|ja|桜井市}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|ja|奈良県}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai-sha|ja|式内社}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社}}. ==Enshrined Deities==
{| class="wikitable" style="font-size:85%; background-color:#ffffff; white-space:nowrap; text-align:center;" |+ Yamato Province – Six Prefecture Shrines ! Prefecture !! {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳}} !! Hiteisha |- | {{ill|Takaichi Prefecture|ja|高市県}} || Takaichi Mikata Shrine || {{ill|Takaichi Mikata Shrine|ja|高市御県神社}} |- | {{ill|Katsuragi Prefecture|ja|葛木県}} || Katsuragi Mikata Shrine || {{ill|Katsuragi Mikata Shrine|ja|葛城御県神社|lt=Katsuragi Mikata Shrine|lt_ja=葛木御縣神社}} |- | {{ill|Juichi Prefecture|ja|十市県}} || Juichi Mikata Shrine || {{ill|Juichi Mikata Shrine|ja|十市御縣坐神社}} |- | {{ill|Shiki Prefecture|ja|志貴県}} || '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' || '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' |- | rowspan="2" | {{ill|Yamabe Prefecture|ja|山辺県}} || rowspan="2" | Yamabe Mikata Shrine || ({{ill|candidate shrines|ja|論社|lt=candidate}}) {{ill|Yamabe Mikata Shrine|ja|山邊御縣神社}} |- || ({{ill|candidate shrines|ja|論社|lt=candidate}}) {{ill|Yamabe Mikata Shrine|ja|山邊御縣神社}} |- | rowspan="2" | {{ill|Sofu Prefecture|ja|曽布県}} || rowspan="2" | Soofu Mikata Shrine || ({{ill|candidate shrines|ja|論社|lt=candidate}}) {{ill|Sofu Mikata Shrine|ja|添御県坐神社}} |- || ({{ill|candidate shrines|ja|論社|lt=candidate}}) {{ill|Sofu Mikata Shrine|ja|添御県坐神社}} |}
The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ōkuninushi|lt_ja=大己貴神}} In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “{{ill|Prefecture Lord|ja|県主|lt=Prefecture Lord|lt_ja=県}} (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}} – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the {{ill|Shinsen Seishiroku|ja|新撰姓氏録}} of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of {{ill|Sendai Kojihonki|ja|先代旧事本紀}} he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|ja|神武天皇}} in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}}, it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城}} – active during the {{ill|Jimmu Eastern Expedition|ja|神武東征}} – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenpyo|ja|天平}} (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of {{ill|Daido|ja|大同}} (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄}}, 12 households from {{ill|Yamato Province|ja|大和国}} were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in {{ill|Rokukokushi|ja|六国史|lt=National History|lt_ja=国史}}, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenan|ja|天安 (日本)|lt=Tenan|lt_ja=天安}} (859) the divine rank ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|lt=Shinkai|ja|神階}}) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|ja|延長 (元号)|lt=Enchō}} (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of {{ill|Bunmei|ja|文明}} (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新}}, under the modern shrine ranking system ({{ill|Modern Shrine Ranking System|ja|近代社格制度}}) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of {{ill|Tenan|ja|天安 (日本)|lt=Tenan|lt_ja=天安}} (859), on {{ill|January 27|ja|1月27日}}, the divine rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録}}) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both {{ill|Kojiki|ja|古事記}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|ja|日本書紀}} as having been established by the 10th-generation {{ill|Emperor Sujin|ja|崇神天皇}}. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名}}, Heibonsha, 1981. File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasus-jinja, honden.jpg|Main Hall File:Legendary Imperial Palace of Emperor Sujin.jpg|Monument of Emperor Sujin's Isoji Mizurubashii Palace File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasus-jinja, 旧[[村社]] |創建 = 不詳 |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan Nara }} '''志貴御縣坐神社'''（しきみあがたにますじんじゃ/しきのみあがたにますじんじゃ、志貴御県坐神社）は、[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]金屋にある[[神社]]。[[式内社]]（[[式内大社]]）で、[[近代社格制度|旧社格]]は[[村社]]。 == 祭神 ==
{| class="wikitable" style="font-size:85%;background-color:#ffffff;white-space: nowrap;text-align:center;" |+大和国六御県神社 !県!!『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]!!比定社 |- |高市県||高市御県神社||[[高市御県神社]] |- |葛木県||葛木御県神社||[[葛城御県神社|葛木御縣神社]] |- |十市県||十市御県坐神社||[[十市御縣坐神社]] |- |志貴県||'''志貴御県坐神社'''||'''志貴御縣坐神社''' |- |rowspan=2|山辺県||rowspan=2|山辺御県坐神社||（論）[[山邊御縣神社 (天理市別所町)|山邊御縣神社]] |- |（論）[[山邊御縣神社 (天理市西井戸堂町)|山邊御縣神社]] |- |rowspan=2|曽布県||rowspan=2|添御県坐神社||（論）[[添御県坐神社 (奈良市歌姫町)|添御県坐神社]] |- |（論）[[添御県坐神社 (奈良市三碓町)|添御県坐神社]] |}
現在の祭神は次の通り（神社明細帳）{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 * [[大国主|大己貴神]] 『大和志料』では祭神を御県の霊とし、その他に天津[[饒速日命]]とする説などがある{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 社名に見える「[[県主|県]]（あがた）」は古代朝廷の直轄地（供御料地）を指す。[[大和国]]の高市・葛木・十市・志貴・山辺・曽布の6県は特に朝廷とのつながりが深く、「[[倭の六県|六御県]]（むつのみあがた）」と総称されて各御県には御県神社が鎮座し、当社はそのうちの1つとされる[[上田正昭]]「六御県」『国史大辞典』吉川弘文館。{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。当社の鎮座する志貴御県の首長は'''磯城県主'''（志貴県主/師木県主：しきのあがたぬし、のち志貴連）で、『[[新撰姓氏録]]』大和国神別 志貴連条では日子湯支命（神饒速日命の孫）の後裔とし、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』「天孫本紀」では建新川命（饒速日命七世孫）または物部印岐美連公（饒速日命七世孫の十市根命の子）の後裔とする{{Sfn|磯城県主（古代氏族）|2010}}。また『[[日本書紀]]』[[神武天皇]]2年条では[[神武東征]]で活躍した[[弟磯城]]を磯城県主にしたと見える{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}{{Sfn|磯城県主（古代氏族）|2010}}。他に磯城県主を[[事代主神]]の後裔とする説があり、過去には[[太田亮]]が「磯城彦は即ち[[三輪氏]]の他ならず」と指摘している宝賀寿男「長髄彦と磯城県主の系譜」『三輪氏　大物主神の祭祀者』青垣出版、2015年。この説を採れば、同神社が大己貴神を祭神としていることにも通じる。 この磯城県主はのちの[[大和国]][[城上郡]]・[[城下郡]]付近に勢力をもった古代豪族とされ、『[[古事記]]』・『日本書紀』では磯城県主[[葉江]]らの娘が[[綏靖天皇]]（第2代）から[[孝霊天皇]]（第7代）までの各天皇の皇后になったとも見えることから、古くから[[ヤマト王権]]と婚姻関係を結んだ様子が示唆される{{Sfn|磯城県主（国史）}}{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}{{Sfn|磯城県主（古代氏族）|2010}}。 == 歴史 == === 概史 === 創建は不詳。 [[天平]]2年（[[730年]]）の『大和国正税帳』では、「志癸御県」の[[神戸 (民戸)|神戸]]として[[城上郡]]内から租穀1,351束8把が定められ、そのうち祭神料として4束が充てられている{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（国史）}}{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 『[[新抄格勅符抄]]』[[大同 (日本)|大同]]元年（[[806年]]）牒では、当時の「志貴御県神」に神戸として[[大和国]]から12戸が充てられている{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（国史）}}{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 [[六国史|国史]]では、[[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）に「志貴御県神」の[[神階]]が従五位下から従五位上に昇叙された旨が記される{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 [[延長 (元号)|延長]]5年（[[927年]]）成立の『[[延喜式]]』[[延喜式神名帳|神名帳]]では、大和国城上郡に「志貴御県坐神社 大 月次新嘗」として、[[式内大社]]に列するとともに、朝廷の[[月次祭]]・[[新嘗祭]]では幣帛に預かる旨が記載されている{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（国史）}}{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 [[文明 (日本)|文明]]6年（[[1474年]]）の「宿院会米帳」には「シキノミヤ」の記載が見える{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 [[明治維新]]後、[[近代社格制度]]では[[村社]]に列している{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（国史）}}{{Sfn|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}。 === 神階 === * [[天安 (日本)|天安]]3年（[[859年]]）[[1月27日]]、従五位下から従五位上（『[[日本三代実録]]』） - 表記は「志貴御県神」。 == 境内 == 志貴御縣坐神社の付近は、一説に『[[古事記]]』・『[[日本書紀]]』に第10代[[崇神天皇]]が営んだと見える[[磯城瑞籬宮]]（師木水垣宮）の跡地に比定され、現在は石碑が建てられている川口勝康「磯城瑞籬宮」『国史大辞典』吉川弘文館。「磯城瑞籬宮」『日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名』平凡社、1981年。。 [[境内社]]に琴平神社と厳島神社がある。拝殿東側には四つの[[磐座]]が等間隔で並んでおり、この場所が古くから信仰の場所であったことを伺わせる。[[毎日新聞]]朝刊、第18面、2024年11月20日。 File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, honden.jpg|本殿 File:Legendary Imperial Palace of Emperor Sujin.jpg|崇神天皇磯城瑞籬宮趾碑 File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, torii.jpg|鳥居 == 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{reflist}} == 参考文献 == * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=|chapter=|title=[[国史大辞典 (昭和時代)|国史大辞典]]|publisher=[[吉川弘文館]]|isbn=|ref=}} ** {{Wikicite|reference=[[真弓常忠]]「磯城県主」|ref={{Harvid|磯城県主（国史）}}}}、{{Wikicite|reference=永島福太郎「志貴御県坐神社」|ref={{Harvid|志貴御県坐神社（国史）}}}}。 * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=1981|chapter=志貴御県坐神社|title=[[日本歴史地名大系]] 30 奈良県の地名|publisher=[[平凡社]]|isbn=4582490301|ref={{Harvid|志貴御県坐神社（平凡社）|1981}}}} * {{Cite book|和書|editor=|author=|year=2010|chapter=磯城県主|title=日本古代氏族人名辞典 普及版|publisher=[[吉川弘文館]]|isbn=978-4642014588|ref={{Harvid|磯城県主（古代氏族）|2010}}}} == 関連項目 == * [[倭の六県]] == 外部リンク == {{Commonscat|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja}} * [http://www.narashinsei.com/search/%E3%82%B5%E8%A1%8C/%E5%BF%97%E8%B2%B4%E5%BE%A1%E7%B8%A3%E5%9D%90%E7%A5%9E%E7%A4%BE/ 志貴御縣坐神社] - 奈良県神社庁 * [http://21coe.kokugakuin.ac.jp/db/jinja/kindex2.php?J_ID=22824 志貴御県坐神社] - 國學院大學21世紀COEプログラム「神道・神社史料集成」 {{神道 横}} {{DEFAULTSORT:しきみあかたにますしんしや}} [[Category:奈良県の神社]] [[Category:桜井市の建築物]] [[Category:桜井市の歴史]] [[Category:大和国の式内社]] [[Category:奈良県の旧村社]] [[Category:山辺の道]]

Lets hope this is sufficient attribution though especially since most of them are mine.[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 08:28, 2 May 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=check [[:en:Draft:Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine]][[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 23:26, 25 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on {{ill|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|ja|Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion|qq=}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by {{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}} {{afc comment|1=Content originally from {{ill|Draft:Moto-Ise Shrines|ja|Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Draft:Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} {{afc comment|1=Grab entry from table ({{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}} to request undeletion of the original page {{ill|draft:Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|ja|draft:Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/draft:Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=}} (see also {{ill|draft:Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|ja|draft:Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/draft:Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=}}). Revisions were imported from EverybodyWiki ({{ill|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|ja|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=}}). – {{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}} ({{ill|User talk:Immanuelle|ja|User talk:Immanuelle|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User talk:Immanuelle|qq=}}) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} as a Wikipedia draft. It was automatically transferred to EverybodyWiki and later recovered. In the future, please import the revisions – check the page history in case the title changed ({{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}}, {{ill|User talk:Immanuelle|ja|User talk:Immanuelle|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User talk:Immanuelle|qq=}}) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} – see that page’s history for attribution ({{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}} ❤️💚💙 {{ill|User_talk:Immanuelle|ja|User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User_talk:Immanuelle|qq=}} 06:22, 3 December 2023 (UTC)}} ❤️💚💙 {{ill|User_talk:Immanuelle|ja|User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User_talk:Immanuelle|qq=}} 06:24, 3 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{神社 |名称 = 志貴御縣坐神社 |image = File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px
Haiden |所在地 = [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]][[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]] Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]].{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]]. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|qq=}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|qq=}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|qq=}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|qq=}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei]] (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], under the modern shrine Ranking system ([[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]]) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|qq=}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1981. In the future, please import the revisions – check the page history in case the title changed ({{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}}, {{ill|User talk:Immanuelle|ja|User talk:Immanuelle|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User talk:Immanuelle|qq=}}) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} – see that page’s history for attribution ({{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}} ❤️💚💙 {{ill|User_talk:Immanuelle|ja|User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User_talk:Immanuelle|qq=}} 06:22, 3 December 2023 (UTC)}} ❤️💚💙 {{ill|User_talk:Immanuelle|ja|User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User_talk:Immanuelle|qq=}} 06:24, 3 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{神社 |名称 = 志貴御縣坐神社 |image = File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px
Haiden |所在地 = [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]][[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]] Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]].{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]]. More sources to add{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Authors |first=Various |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534 |title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols) |date=2021-03-18 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-90356-4 |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107 |title=Where the Trees Grow Thick |isbn=978-0-595-28240-1 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last1=Göttler |first1=Christine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437 |title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art |last2=Mochizuki |first2=Mia |date=2017-11-06 |publisher=BRILL |isbn=978-90-04-35450-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|qq=}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|qq=}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|qq=}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|qq=}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei]] (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], under the modern shrine Ranking system ([[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]]) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|qq=}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1981. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|qq=}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|qq=}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|qq=}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|qq=}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Revisions were imported from EverybodyWiki ({{ill|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|ja|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine|qq=}}). – {{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}} ({{ill|User talk:Immanuelle|ja|User talk:Immanuelle|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User talk:Immanuelle|qq=}}) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} as a Wikipedia draft. In the future, please import the revisions – check the page history in case the title changed ({{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}}, {{ill|User talk:Immanuelle|ja|User talk:Immanuelle|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User talk:Immanuelle|qq=}}) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} – see that page’s history for attribution ({{ill|User:Immanuelle|ja|User:Immanuelle|lt='''Immanuel'''le|lt_ja='''Immanuel'''le|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User:Immanuelle|qq=}} ❤️💚💙 {{ill|User_talk:Immanuelle|ja|User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User_talk:Immanuelle|qq=}} 06:22, 3 December 2023 (UTC)}} ❤️💚💙 {{ill|User_talk:Immanuelle|ja|User_talk:Immanuelle|(talk to the cutest Wikipedian)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/User_talk:Immanuelle|qq=}} 06:24, 3 December 2023 (UTC)}} {{神社 |名称 = 志貴御縣坐神社 |image = File:Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg|280px
Haiden |所在地 = [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]][[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]] Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]].{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]]. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|qq=}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|qq=}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|qq=}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|qq=}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|qq=}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei]] (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], under the modern shrine Ranking system ([[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]]) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|qq=}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|qq=}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Haiden |所在地 = [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]][[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]] Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]].{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|qid=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]].
