The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei]] (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], under the modern shrine Ranking system ([[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]]) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Haiden |所在地 = [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]][[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]] Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]].{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社}} ([[:en:Ōmiwa Shrine|Ōmiwa Shrine]]).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]]. More sources to add{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Authors |first=Various |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534 |title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols) |date=2021-03-18 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-90356-4 |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107 |title=Where the Trees Grow Thick |isbn=978-0-595-28240-1 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last1=Göttler |first1=Christine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437 |title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art |last2=Mochizuki |first2=Mia |date=2017-11-06 |publisher=BRILL |isbn=978-90-04-35450-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Army |first=United States Department of the |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PvgsAAAAIAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=RA3-PA147 |title=Pamphlet - Dept. of the Army |date=1945 |publisher=Headquarters, Department of the Army. |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MVHoAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA147 |title=Department of the Army Pamphlet |date=1945 |publisher=The Department |language=en}} ==Enshrined Deities==

Miagata Niimasu Shrine|qq=}} |}
The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei]] (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], under the modern shrine Ranking system ([[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]]) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei]] (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], under the modern shrine Ranking system ([[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]]) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Haiden |所在地 = [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]][[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]] Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to [[:en:Ise Shrine|Ise Jingu]].{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in [[:en:Sakurai, Nara|Sakurai City]], [[:en:Nara Prefecture|Nara Prefecture]]. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * [[:en:Ōkuninushi|Ōkuninushi]] In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “[[:en:Agatanushi|Prefecture Lord]] (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the [[:en:Shinsen Shōjiroku|Shinsen Seishiroku]] of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of [[:en:Kujiki|Sendai Kojihonki]] he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for [[:en:Emperor Jimmu|Emperor Jimmu]] in [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]], it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the [[:en:Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|Jimmu Eastern Expedition]] – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of [[:en:Tenpyō|Tenpyo]] (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of [[:en:Datong (disambiguation)|Daido]] (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from [[:en:Yamato Province|Yamato Province]] were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in [[:en:Rikkokushi|National History]], in the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859) the divine Rank ([[:en:Shinkai (divine rank)|Shinkai]]) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of [[:en:Enchō|Enchō]] (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of [[:en:Civilization|Bunmei]] (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the [[:en:Meiji Restoration|Meiji Restoration]], under the modern shrine Ranking system ([[:en:Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines]]) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of [[:en:Ten'an|Tenan]] (859), on [[:en:January 27|January 27]], the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in [[:en:Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku]]) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both [[:en:Kojiki|Kojiki]] and [[:en:Nihon Shoki|Nihon Shoki]] as having been established by the 10th-generation [[:en:Emperor Sujin|Emperor Sujin]]. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Haiden |所在地 = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}{{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City}} Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingu}}.{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingu}}. More sources to add{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Authors |first=Various |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534 |title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols) |date=2021-03-18 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-90356-4 |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107 |title=Where the Trees Grow Thick |isbn=978-0-595-28240-1 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last1=Göttler |first1=Christine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437 |title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art |last2=Mochizuki |first2=Mia |date=2017-11-06 |publisher=BRILL |isbn=978-90-04-35450-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “{{ill|Agatanushi|en|Agatanushi|WD=Q10746487|lt=Prefecture Lord}} (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|WD=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Seishiroku}} of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|WD=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kojihonki}} he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|WD=Q11590444|lt=Jimmu Eastern Expedition}} – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|WD=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyo}} (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daido}} (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|WD=Q1151168|lt=National History}}, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|en|Ten'an|WD=Q1075611|lt=Tenan}} (859) the divine Rank ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|en|Shinkai (divine rank)|WD=Q11591025|lt=Shinkai}}) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|en|Enchō|WD=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of {{ill|Civilization|en|Civilization|WD=Q8432|lt=Bunmei}} (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|WD=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}, under the modern shrine Ranking system ({{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|en|Ten'an|WD=Q1075611|lt=Tenan}} (859), on {{ill|January 27|en|January 27|WD=Q2284|lt=January 27}}, the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} as having been established by the 10th-generation {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Haiden |所在地 = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}{{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City}} Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingu}}.{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingu}}. More sources to add{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Authors |first=Various |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XEIiEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA534 |title=RLE: Japan Mini-Set F: Philosophy and Religion (4 vols) |date=2021-03-18 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-90356-4 |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=nPaezHFlfNQC&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PT107 |title=Where the Trees Grow Thick |isbn=978-0-595-28240-1 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last1=Göttler |first1=Christine |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uyk_DwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA437 |title=The Nomadic Object: The Challenge of World for Early Modern Religious Art |last2=Mochizuki |first2=Mia |date=2017-11-06 |publisher=BRILL |isbn=978-90-04-35450-0 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. A. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BY23AwAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA555 |title=Studies In Shinto & Shrines |date=2014-06-03 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-136-89294-3 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Army |first=United States Department of the |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=PvgsAAAAIAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=RA3-PA147 |title=Pamphlet - Dept. of the Army |date=1945 |publisher=Headquarters, Department of the Army. |language=en}}{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MVHoAAAAMAAJ&dq=%22Moto+Ise%22&pg=PA147 |title=Department of the Army Pamphlet |date=1945 |publisher=The Department |language=en}} ==Enshrined Deities==

The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “{{ill|Agatanushi|en|Agatanushi|WD=Q10746487|lt=Prefecture Lord}} (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|WD=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Seishiroku}} of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|WD=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kojihonki}} he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|WD=Q11590444|lt=Jimmu Eastern Expedition}} – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|WD=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyo}} (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daido}} (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|WD=Q1151168|lt=National History}}, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|en|Ten'an|WD=Q1075611|lt=Tenan}} (859) the divine Rank ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|en|Shinkai (divine rank)|WD=Q11591025|lt=Shinkai}}) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|en|Enchō|WD=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of {{ill|Civilization|en|Civilization|WD=Q8432|lt=Bunmei}} (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|WD=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}, under the modern shrine Ranking system ({{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|en|Ten'an|WD=Q1075611|lt=Tenan}} (859), on {{ill|January 27|en|January 27|WD=Q2284|lt=January 27}}, the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} as having been established by the 10th-generation {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1981. Haiden |所在地 = {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}{{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City}} Kanaya 896 |緯度度 = 34 |緯度分 = 31 |緯度秒 = 31.18 |経度度 = 135 |経度分 = 51 |経度秒 = 10.37 |ISO = JP-29 |祭神 = {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} |神体 = |社格 = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}})
Formerly {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}} |創建 = Unknown |例祭 = |本殿 = |別名 = |札所等 = |神事 = |ラベル位置 = top |地図 = Japan, Nara |ja|Shiki-no-miagatanimasu-jinja, haiden.jpg }} '''Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine''' (志貴御縣坐神社) is a {{ill|Moto-Ise Shrines|lt=Moto-Ise Shrine|ja|元伊勢|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Moto-Ise Shrines|qq=}} that once housed [[Amaterasu]], [[Shintai|via the Yata-no-Kagami and the Kusanagi sword]], before she was moved to {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingu}}.{{Cite book |last=Kidder |first=J. Edward |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7pEOicqsjv0C&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA201 |title=Himiko and Japan's Elusive Chiefdom of Yamatai: Archaeology, History, and Mythology |date=2007-02-28 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-3035-9 |language=en}}{{Cite book |last=Stalker |first=Nancy K. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=v44BEAAAQBAJ&dq=%22Moto-Ise%22&pg=PA62 |title=Prophet Motive: Deguchi Onisaburō, Oomoto, and the Rise of New Religions in Imperial Japan |date=2007-10-31 |publisher=University of Hawaii Press |isbn=978-0-8248-6404-0 |language=en}} It is located at Kanaya 896 in {{ill|Sakurai, Nara|en|Sakurai, Nara|WD=Q127026|lt=Sakurai City}}, {{ill|Nara Prefecture|en|Nara Prefecture|WD=Q131287|lt=Nara Prefecture}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}}) whose former status was that of a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}. == Background == The first shrine was {{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|lt=Hibara Shrine|ja|檜原神社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa Shrine|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神神社}} ({{ill|Ōmiwa Shrine|en|Ōmiwa Shrine|WD=Q705542|lt=Ōmiwa Shrine}}).{{Cite web |last=D |first=John |date=2011-08-10 |title=Hibara Jinja and Amaterasu |url=https://www.greenshinto.com/2011/08/11/hibara-jinja-and-amaterasu/ |access-date=2023-10-18 |website=Green Shinto |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |title=Hibara Jinja Shrine（Nara） |url=https://www.jldb.bunka.go.jp/en/location/290100006/?search=1&q=Hibara+Shrine |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=Nationwide location database |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=Omiwa Jinja Shrine/Sai Jinja Shrine/Kuehiko Jinja Shrine/Hibara Jinja Shrine│Destinations│Discover YAMATO│YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |url=http://www.city.sakurai.lg.jp/section/yamato-travel/destination/area01/spot02/ |access-date=2023-10-03 |website=YAMATO UNKNOWN ORIGIN |language=en}} Amaterasu was originally enshrined there before eventually being transferred to other Moto-Ise shrines and finally to {{ill|Ise Shrine|en|Ise Shrine|WD=Q687168|lt=Ise Jingu}}. The current enshrined deity, according to the Shrine Register,{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} is: * {{ill|Ōkuninushi|en|Ōkuninushi|WD=Q276944|lt=Ōkuninushi}} In the "Yamato Shiryō" the deity is regarded as the spirit of the prefecture, with some theories also including Amatsu {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} The term “{{ill|Agatanushi|en|Agatanushi|WD=Q10746487|lt=Prefecture Lord}} (agata)” appearing in the shrine’s name refers to land under the direct control of the ancient court (kugoryo territory). The six prefectures of {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} – Takaichi, Katsuragi, Juichi, Shiki, Yamabe, and Sofu – had especially close ties with the court. Collectively known as {{ill|Mutsunomiagata|ja|倭の六県|lt=Mutsunomiagata|lt_ja=六御県|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mutsunomiagata|qq=}} (read “mutsunomiagata”), each prefecture had its own mikata shrine, with this shrine being one among them.{{ill|Ueda Masaaki|ja|上田正昭|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ueda Masaaki|qq=}} "Rokugoken" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}. The head of the prefecture where this shrine is enshrined is '''Isoji Kengunushi''' (also known as Shiki Kengunushi or Shiki no Agatanushi, later Shikiren). In the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|WD=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Seishiroku}} of Yamato Province, the deity is identified as a descendant of Hikoyudenshin (the grandson of {{ill|Nagasohito|ja|饒速日命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nagasohito|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to ニギハヤヒ}}), while in the "Tenson Hongi" of {{ill|Kujiki|en|Kujiki|WD=Q2716751|lt=Sendai Kojihonki}} he is described as a descendant of either Kenshinkawa-no-mikoto (the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito) or of Mononobe Inabamiren-kō (the child of Juichi-ne no Mikoto, the seventh-generation descendant of Nagasohito).{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Furthermore, in the 2nd year entry for {{ill|Emperor Jimmu|en|Emperor Jimmu|WD=Q200188|lt=Emperor Jimmu}} in {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}}, it appears that the warrior {{ill|Otoko Isoji|ja|弟磯城|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Otoko Isoji|qq=}} – active during the {{ill|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|en|Jimmu's Eastern Expedition|WD=Q11590444|lt=Jimmu Eastern Expedition}} – was designated Isoji Kengunushi.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}}{{Sfn|Isoji Kengunushi (Ancient Clan)|2010}} Another theory holds that Isoji Kengunushi is a descendant of {{ill|Kotoshiro-nushi|ja|事代主神|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotoshiro-nushi|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 事代主}}, with past scholar {{ill|Ota Ryo|ja|太田亮|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ota Ryo|qq=}} having remarked that “Isoji no Oji is none other than the {{ill|Miwa clan|ja|三輪氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miwa clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 大神氏}}.”{{ill|Takaraga Hisao|ja|宝賀寿男|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takaraga Hisao|qq=}} "Naganarihiko and the Genealogy of Isoji Kengunushi" in ''Miwa-shi: Worshippers of Ōmononushi'', Aogaki Publishing, 2015. If this theory is adopted, it would also explain why the shrine enshrines Ōkuninushi. ==History== ===General History=== The founding date is unknown. In the 2nd year of {{ill|Tenpyō|en|Tenpyō|WD=Q1199879|lt=Tenpyo}} (730), the "Yamato Province Shōzei Chō" records list “Shiki no Mikata” as a divine gate ({{ill|Kamibe|ja|神戸 (民戸)|lt=Kamibe|lt_ja=神戸|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kamibe|qq=}}) drawn from within {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a total allotment of 1,351 bundles and 8 units of tax rice – of which 4 bundles were allocated for the enshrinement fee.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 1st year of {{ill|Datong (disambiguation)|en|Datong (disambiguation)|WD=Q295082|lt=Daido}} (806) according to the imperial edict recorded in {{ill|Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|ja|新抄格勅符抄|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinshō Kakuchofu-sho|qq=}}, 12 households from {{ill|Yamato Province|en|Yamato Province|WD=Q907495|lt=Yamato Province}} were assigned as the divine gate for “Shiki no Mikata God”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} According to the history in {{ill|Rikkokushi|en|Rikkokushi|WD=Q1151168|lt=National History}}, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|en|Ten'an|WD=Q1075611|lt=Tenan}} (859) the divine Rank ({{ill|Shinkai (divine rank)|en|Shinkai (divine rank)|WD=Q11591025|lt=Shinkai}}) of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 5th year of {{ill|Enchō|en|Enchō|WD=Q1327274|lt=Enchō}} (927), as recorded in the established {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, the shrine – listed as “Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine, Great Tsukiji Niinamesai” – was placed among the {{ill|Shikinai-taisha|ja|式内大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinai-taisha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 名神大社}} in {{ill|Jokō District|ja|城上郡|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jokō District|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 式上郡}}, with a note that offerings of cloth and ritual paper were received at the court’s monthly and Niinamesai festivals.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} In the 6th year of {{ill|Civilization|en|Civilization|WD=Q8432|lt=Bunmei}} (1474), the "Shukuin-kai Beichō" makes a reference to “Shikinomiya”.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|en|Meiji Restoration|WD=Q8707|lt=Meiji Restoration}}, under the modern shrine Ranking system ({{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|WD=Q712534|lt=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}) the shrine was classified as a {{ill|Sonsha|ja|村社|1=Son-sha|WD=Q134917284}}{{efn|Former shrine rank|lt=Son-sha|1=Modern_system_of_ranked_Shinto_shrines#Village_shrines|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sonsha|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 近代社格制度}}.{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (National History)}}{{Sfn|Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1981}} ===Divine Rank=== * In the 3rd year of {{ill|Ten'an|en|Ten'an|WD=Q1075611|lt=Tenan}} (859), on {{ill|January 27|en|January 27|WD=Q2284|lt=January 27}}, the divine Rank of “Shiki no Mikata God” was raised from Junior Fifth Rank Lower to Junior Fifth Rank Upper (as recorded in {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|en|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|WD=Q1052981|lt=Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku}}) – the inscription reads “志貴御県神”. ==Shrine Grounds== The area surrounding Shiki no Miagata Nimasu Shrine is, according to one theory, identified with the site of {{ill|Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|ja|磯城瑞籬宮|lt=Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isoji Mizurubashii Palace|qq=}} (also known as Shiki Mizugaki Palace), which is mentioned in both {{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|WD=Q813031|lt=Kojiki}} and {{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|WD=Q813935|lt=Nihon Shoki}} as having been established by the 10th-generation {{ill|Emperor Sujin|en|Emperor Sujin|WD=Q333530|lt=Emperor Sujin}}. A stone monument now stands on the site.{{ill|Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja|川口勝康|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawaguchi Katsuyasu|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} "Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Kokushi Daijiten|ja|国史大辞典|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kokushi Daijiten|qq=}}, Yoshikawa Kōbunkan."Isoji Mizurubashii Palace" in {{ill|Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja|日本歴史地名大系 30 奈良県の地名|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Rekishi Chimei Taikei 30: Place Names of Nara Prefecture|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}}, Heibonsha, 1981.
